what: Today's scheduled CI, serving both versions: PR 1570's changed leg 2 waited 705 seconds, from 15:14:09Z to 15:25:54Z. Its shared group 2 was executing earlier jobs for 702 seconds. Group 6 had no executing or already-created waiting job for the final 286 seconds. Across all nine groups, empty groups added up to 780 group-seconds during that wait. This measures shared group use, not free hosted machines.
cause: Changed legs use their number as their shared group. Full browser leg 2 also used group 2 and ended at 15:25:53Z; the proof leg started one second later. Full core leg 4 released group 6 at 15:21:08Z. All 215 retained scheduled-run records created before the wait ended were examined; five overlapped the wider 15:13:00Z to 15:25:54Z interval, all on attempt 1 with byte-identical shared-group workflow definitions.
fix: Swap the full matrix's browser leg 2 and core leg 4 group assignments, 2 and 6. Keep the same nine distinct test groups and one control group. This changes who waits behind whom; it does not provide first-free scheduling or establish a future speedup.
test: Existing SC19 laws accept every permutation of the nine full-matrix groups and reject missing, duplicate and private groups. New actual CI comparison is still owed. No historical proof is relabeled.
